sections.h2: DeKalb County offices for value and billing
sections.html:
Two separate offices split the job. The Property Appraisal Department sets what your home is worth. The Tax Commissioner's Office then sends the bill and takes payment, and it has no say over the assessed amount.

The DeKalb County Board of Commissioners adopts the millage rate each July. The Tax Commissioner's central property tax office is staffed weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. at 404-298-4000. Call the Property Appraisal Department at 404-371-0841 about a value or a missing assessment notice.

Cities add their own levies. Atlanta, Brookhaven, Chamblee, Clarkston, Decatur, Doraville, Dunwoody, Lithonia, Pine Lake, Stone Mountain, Stonecrest and Tucker each have local exemption rules, and Avondale does not award local exemptions.

Bills go out in August, and the installment dates are September 30 and November 15. Paying in one lump sum means paying by September 30. If a deadline falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it moves to Monday.

The penalty for a late first or second installment is 5%, and a postmark after the date triggers it. Metered and kiosk postage dates are not accepted as proof, so near a deadline ask the post office to hand-cancel the envelope. Online payments must arrive by midnight on the deadline, Eastern time.

Balances still open 120 days after the deadline pick up a further 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days. Accounts with a balance after December 31 become subject to a lien.

sections.h2: Ways to pay a DeKalb tax bill
sections.html:
Current-year payments can be mailed to DeKalb County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division, P.O. Box 117545, Atlanta, GA 30368-7545. Prior-year payments go to the Delinquent Collections Division, P.O. Box 100001, Decatur, GA 30031-7001. Checks must be in U.S. funds.

  • Phone: 678-501-7995, with no fee for an e-check
  • Online: the county's GovHub payment portal, searchable by parcel ID, address or owner name
  • Card: a 2.31% fee with a $1.50 minimum per transaction; international and commercial cards add 3.95%
  • A returned payment costs 5% of the check with a $30 minimum

Partial payments are accepted, and the first installment must be paid before the second. The portal handles real estate and business personal property accounts only. Mobile home, public utility and heavy equipment accounts go by mail or to a county counter.

sections.h2: How to contest a DeKalb County assessment
sections.html:
Read the May assessment notice and count 45 days from the date printed on it. The filing instructions come with the notice. State law lets the appeal rest on value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption, filed in writing with the board of assessors.

Georgia offers three tracks: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer for non-homestead property valued above $500,000, or arbitration for value. A taxpayer still unhappy can file a notice of appeal for superior court inside 30 days of the decision, once taxes equal to the last year's amount are paid, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-29 requires.

An unresolved appeal does not stop the bill. DeKalb issues a temporary value, normally the lesser of the last final value or 85 percent of the current value. You can ask in your appeal to be billed at 100 percent instead. Interest applies to appeal differences settled after November 15, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-311(e)(6) provides.

To claim the basic homestead exemption you must occupy the house as your main home on January 1 and hold title. You also need every vehicle registered at that address, a Georgia ID or license showing the property address, income taxes filed from the home, and no homestead claim anywhere else. Applications are not automatic, and neither a lender nor a closing attorney files one for you.

  • Special exemptions exist for owners 62 and older, disabled residents and disabled veteran owners, and several depend on income
  • An applicant must already hold a homestead exemption to add a special one
  • Applications are taken in person year-round and online from January 1 to mid-July
  • A county assessment freeze is available when you apply by April 1, and it does not cover school, city or state taxes

City programs differ. Brookhaven has a $40,000 basic exemption, Chamblee $50,000, and Doraville $10,000 plus a 2.5 mill reduction. Clarkston gives homeowners 65 and older an extra $20,000. Decatur and Stone Mountain take applications at city hall rather than through the county.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a house sells mid-year?
sections.html:
Taxes follow the property, and Georgia sets the year-long liability at January 1. Whoever held the parcel on January 1 owes the full year, however soon after the sale closes. The January 1 owner of record gets the mailed bill, and a buyer whose deed is recorded afterward gets one too.

Who actually pays is a contract matter. New owners should check with the closing attorney, mortgage company or escrow agent, or read the closing statement. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the parcel, and DeKalb does not send bills to mortgage lenders, so an escrow account does not remove your duty to confirm payment.

Before listing, pull your parcel on the payment portal and confirm nothing is open. A parcel with a balance after December 31 can be liened, and the lien, called a FiFa, is the first step toward a tax sale. Sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month in front of the DeKalb County Courthouse, and buyers pay with cash, a bank-issued cashier's check or a wire. Money left over after taxes and costs is held as excess funds until an entitled party claims it.

DeKalb County had an estimated 774,394 people in mid-2025, a 1.3% gain on the April 2020 base, living in 287,239 households. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,979, and those without one $715. Owners on fixed incomes should look at the senior and income-based exemptions.

Start with the parcel lookup on the payment portal and print the balance. If the first installment is unpaid, pay it before the second. Ask the closing attorney or escrow agent to confirm in writing who covers the part of the year after closing, and keep the receipt for any payment you make.

If you filed for a homestead exemption, the buyer will need to apply on their own for the next year, since nothing carries over automatically. A cash buyer skips the lender's tax certification, but the title search will still show any open balance or lien, so clear it before the closing date.

faqs.q: When is the second DeKalb County property tax installment due?
faqs.a: November 15, shifted to Monday when it lands on a Saturday or Sunday. A late payment carries a 5% penalty if the envelope is not postmarked by the due date.

faqs.q: Which office explains a DeKalb assessed value?
faqs.a: The Property Appraisal Department, at 404-371-0841. The Tax Commissioner's Office, at 404-298-4000, handles billing and has no authority over the value.

faqs.q: Can I pay my DeKalb tax bill in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The county splits the bill into two installments, due September 30 and November 15, and the first must be paid before the second. Paying everything at once means paying by September 30.

faqs.q: Does the DeKalb homestead exemption apply automatically?
faqs.a: No. You must file an application, and a missed filing waives the exemption for that year under O.C.G.A. 48-5-45(a)(2). You can apply for the following year if you miss the cutoff.

faqs.q: What follows when DeKalb property taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: Penalties and interest build, a lien can be filed after December 31, and the lien is the first step toward a tax sale. Pay the balance with fees and the lien is marked satisfied.
